summary: Honduras's own per-nationality visa list is no longer online, so this page gives the entry rule only for passports an official source still states. The National Institute of Migration says a tourist may stay up to 90 days, extendable by 30 days, and distinguishes a consular visa from a "consulted" visa that it must authorise first. Citizens of Guatemala, El Salvador and Nicaragua can enter with a national identity card or a passport under the CA-4 agreement. An online immigration pre-check can be completed before arrival.

declarations.name: Online immigration pre-check (Prechequeo Migratorio)
declarations.text: Honduras's National Migration Institute runs an online immigration pre-check (prechequeo) for both entry and exit at prechequeo.inm.gob.hn: you request a one-time token by email, submit your details for approval, and can download the approved pre-check to show the immigration officer. No official source we could read says whether it is mandatory.

declarations.text: Every traveller, Honduran or foreign, entering or leaving Honduras by air, sea or land must present the customs Regional Traveller's Sworn Declaration, stating whether they carry cash or other instruments worth USD 10,000 or more. It is filled in online on the customs portal; the UK government says to complete it before entering or leaving and show the QR code to customs, on paper or on screen.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says Honduras has one of the highest violent crime rates in Latin America, though most serious crime does not affect tourists. It advises avoiding walking around Tegucigalpa, San Pedro Sula and other mainland cities, using radio-dispatched or hotel taxis for short distances, not displaying valuables and avoiding road travel at night. Canada's travel advice says the Bay Islands are generally safe, with lower violent crime.

tips.text: You can complete the online prechequeo at prechequeo.inm.gob.hn before you fly, for arrival and again for departure, and download the approved pre-check to show the immigration officer. Whether it is mandatory is not officially stated.

Canada's travel advice says Canadians can travel between Honduras, Guatemala, El Salvador and Nicaragua (the CA-4) for up to 90 days, that an extension of up to 30 days must be requested from the National Institute of Migration before the first stay expires, and that Honduras allows a maximum of 120 days.

If you dive in the Bay Islands, the UK FCDO says there is a hyperbaric (recompression) chamber on Roatán and recompression facilities on Utila, but that emergency medical facilities on the islands are extremely limited.

The UK FCDO advises avoiding walking around Tegucigalpa, San Pedro Sula and other mainland cities, using radio-dispatched or hotel taxis for short distances, considering alternatives to public buses, and not displaying phones, jewellery or other valuables.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Honduras?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport, and Honduras's own per-nationality visa list is no longer online. Foreign governments' travel advice says Canadian, Dutch and Italian citizens need no visa for stays of up to 90 days, and the UK Foreign Office says British citizens must have one. The National Institute of Migration says tourists may stay up to 90 days, extendable by 30, and distinguishes a consular visa from a "consulted" visa that it must authorise first.

faq.question: What is the Honduras prechequeo form?
faq.answer: An online immigration pre-check run by Honduras's National Migration Institute at prechequeo.inm.gob.hn, for entry or exit. You request a one-time token by email, submit your details for approval and can download the result to show the immigration officer. No official source we could read says whether it is mandatory.

faq.question: How does the CA-4 90-day rule work in Honduras?
faq.answer: Canada's travel advice says that under the CA-4 agreement Canadians can travel between Honduras, Guatemala, El Salvador and Nicaragua for up to 90 days, with the length of stay set by the officer at the first entry point. An extension of up to 30 days must be requested and paid for at the National Institute of Migration before the first stay expires, and Honduras allows a maximum of 120 days; after that you must change your status, leave the CA-4 region or travel to El Salvador.

faq.question: Is Honduras safe for tourists?
faq.answer: The UK FCDO says Honduras has one of the highest violent crime rates in Latin America; most serious crime does not affect tourists, but incidents can happen anywhere, including tourist areas. Canada says the Bay Islands are generally safe, with lower violent crime, and advises avoiding non-essential travel to some areas, including within 20 km of the borders with Guatemala and El Salvador (Copán Ruinas and the El Florido crossing are excluded) and parts of San Pedro Sula. Both advise against road travel at night.

faq.question: Can I pay in US dollars on Roatán?
faq.answer: The UK FCDO says US dollars are widely accepted for exchange and payment in Honduras, and that British pounds are difficult to exchange. It advises checking with your hotel which ATMs to use, especially on Roatán.
